copy.aboutLead: I'm a Unity developer transitioning into gameplay programming, with seven years of professional experience in sound engineering.
copy.aboutParagraph1: My professional background is in live sound reinforcement, system engineering, and studio production. Working in these environments gave me extensive practical experience with signal flow, acoustic systems, technical problem solving, and real-time production workflows.
copy.aboutParagraph2: I'm currently focused on gameplay programming with Unity and C#. Through personal projects, I've been developing state-driven gameplay systems, combat mechanics, enemy behavior, and data-driven architectures. These projects have also given me opportunities to explore code organization, system design, and development workflows.
copy.focusAreas: Unity & C#, Gameplay Programming, Data-Driven Design, State Machines, Development Tools, FMOD, Procedural Acoustics, Adaptive Music
copy.principlesText: Learning gameplay programming in Unity and C#, alongside game audio projects in FMOD.
copy.aboutParagraph3: Alongside gameplay programming, I continue working with interactive audio using FMOD. My technical audio projects include adaptive music systems, procedural room acoustics, reverb, and source occlusion. This work allows me to apply my professional audio experience in a game development environment.
copy.aboutParagraph4: My long-term goal is to become a stronger software developer while continuing to build on my background in audio engineering. I'm particularly interested in the intersection of gameplay systems, real-time audio, and technical implementation.
copy.projectsProgrammingDetails: Unity and C# projects covering gameplay programming, game architecture and development tools. This section also includes FMOD projects on adaptive music and procedural acoustics. Select a project for its video, implementation notes and source links.
copy.projectsAudioDetails: Linear sound redesigns for gameplay and cinematic sequences. Select a project to watch the video and read its production notes and source-audio credits.
